# <ID>: <Technique name>

Status: planned | in_progress | implemented | validated | blocked
Catalog status: accepted | proposed | rejected | deprecated

## Problem and intuition
Explain in plain language with one concrete question/document. Explain required terms before using them.

## Inputs, outputs and mechanism
List data contracts and a short step-by-step flow. Add a compact diagram only if useful.

## Primary source and fidelity
Official documentation/original paper, version/date checked; faithful/adapted/simulated; list deviations. Explain resource/model assumptions.

## Implementation map
Actual files and entrypoint, strategy ID, dependencies and compatible indexes. No imaginary commands.

## Worked demonstration
Small authorized fixture, expected intermediate output, actual observed output and source mapping.

## Failure case
Show a meaningful limitation or regression. Explain why it happens.

## Verification
Contract, provenance and relevant security/error tests; exact commands/results.

## Experiment
Dataset/corpus/index/config/model/code versions; baseline; controlled variable; per-case evidence; metrics; cost/latency/storage; repetitions; interpretation.

## Selection guidance
When it helps, when it hurts, dependencies and interactions with other techniques. Production eligibility is separate from learning completion.

## Learner checkpoint
One explain-back question, one output to inspect, one small parameter change to predict and try. This is a learning aid, not a mandatory permission gate.

## Plugin and catalogue record
Catalogue ID, category, plugin kind, fidelity (faithful/adaptation/simulation), required capabilities (provider flags and infrastructure), config schema, `roadmap_step`, `primary_source`, `date_added`. Keep `config/techniques.json` and `docs/techniques/TECHNIQUE_CATALOG.md` in sync.
